utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: There's no question, sir, that Mr. Kordic did not have individual political power in your municipality, did he? You only ever saw him there, I think, once and that was in 1992. He wasn't, in any sense, the leading Croat politician in Travnik, was he?

utterances.speaker: HALID GENJAC
utterances.text: What I do know is that Mr. Kordic filled different offices. He was the Vice-President of the Croat Republic of Herceg-Bosna/Croat Community of Herceg-Bosna, Vice-President of the HDZ, and as such, I know that local leaders asked him, invited him and asked -- invited his opinion because they frequently quoted Mr. Kordic at various meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: With the sole exception of January of 1993, would it be fair to say that, as far as you were aware, Mr. Kordic did not set foot in the municipality of Travnik from June of 1992 until the signature of the Washington Agreement?

utterances.speaker: HALID GENJAC
utterances.text: I cannot remember every detail. However, I do know that the municipal mayor told me that Mr. Kordic arrived in front of the municipal hall in Travnik in an APC, but I don't know when that was exactly. There was some incident about the entrance into the municipal hall, municipal building. I did not eyewitness that and I do not know, but I heard about that. There were some other situations mentioned where Mr. Kordic did come to Travnik, but I was not present there and I did not see that with my own eyes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Thank you very much. No further questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I have no questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Just a couple of points, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Dr. Genjac, your comment about the Croat exodus as a scenario planned in advance, what was your understanding of who planned the scenario? How did you view this?

utterances.speaker: HALID GENJAC
utterances.text: I think it was all planned by the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: The reference made to the HVO -- to acknowledging the existence of the HVO as a military force in Bosnia between Mr. Izetbegovic and Mr. Boban, you began to indicate that that was as to a military force. Are you aware of any document or any agreement made by any leader of the legitimate Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina giving away to the HVO any executive, administrative, legal powers? Are you aware of any such agreement?

utterances.speaker: HALID GENJAC
utterances.text: I do not know of any decision of any substance of that; quite the contrary. All we know about are the decisions of the Constitutional Court which annulled both the decision of the establishment of the Croat Republic of Herceg-Bosna and all the decisions emerging from that, and naturally the decision on the establishment of the Croat community of Herceg-Bosna and all the decisions deriving from there.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And just finally if I can confirm, the description as temporary, that you indicated was given to you on a number of occasions by Dario Kordic, do you have an opinion on whether or not the subsequent evolution of the community of Herceg-Bosna, HZ HB, progressing to a republic of Herceg-Bosna, HR HB, suggested temporariness or permanence?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Well, I object to that on the grounds that that calls for just a naked opinion, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We allow many questions which would frequently be disallowed. This one we will not allow.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: No further questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Dr. Genjac, thank you for coming to the Tribunal to give your evidence. It's now concluded and you are free to go.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Tomorrow morning, then, we will discuss the matters which have been raised and try and deal with all of the administrative matters which are outstanding, with a view to concluding this case. Half past nine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
